items.title: Run the CLI through a symlinked path (npm .bin link, node_modules/<pkg> under pnpm)
body: npm installs `bin` as a symlink `node_modules/.bin/houserules -> ../houserules/bin/houserules.mjs`. Node resolves `import.meta.url` through the symlink but keeps `process.argv[1]` as the `.bin` path, so the entry guard in `bin/houserules.mjs` never matches and the CLI exits 0 without output.

Fix: compare against `realpathSync(process.argv[1])` in the guard; apply the same idiom in `template/tools/kb.mjs` and `template/tools/backlog.mjs`. Regression test: run the bin through a symlink and expect the manifest.
Verified live on 2026-08-31 with `npm exec --package=git+file://<clone> -- houserules files`: 0 lines, exit 0; the direct path prints the manifest.

Probe of 2026-09-01 under pnpm 11.18.0 (`pnpm add --save-exact git+file://<clone>` in a scratch project): `pnpm exec houserules files` and `pnpm dlx git+file://<clone> files` print the manifest, because pnpm's bin shim execs the real path under `node_modules/.pnpm/`; `node node_modules/houserules/bin/houserules.mjs files` through the package symlink prints nothing and exits 0. The defect is independent of the package manager.

items.title: Report invalid JSON in knowledge and backlog files as a usage error
body: `loadBase` and `loadBacklog` let `JSON.parse` errors escape as stack traces (`SyntaxError: Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1`); `tools/kb.sh render` inside `init` then dies with the raw trace.

Fix: `readJson` raises a `UsageError` that names the file and the parse message, as `audit --report` already does for a malformed report. `init` keeps failing with a non-zero exit; the init test `lets a render failure on broken project data propagate as a real error` stays valid.

items.title: Port process.evals-rerun with its co-change check and evals record from tag-pilot
body: tag-pilot `fc3241b` (2026-08-31) adds the rule `process.evals-rerun`: re-run every `.claude/evals/` scenario whenever the implementer or task-reviewer template or a scenario changes; a `co-change` check fails the audit until `.claude/evals/record.json` changes with them; the record keys runs by the templates' git blob ids. The orchestrating skill gains a 'Template evaluation' procedure and the branch reviewer compares the record's blob ids with HEAD.

Blocked until PR #42 is merged (owner instruction). Then port it to `template/` (knowledge entry, orchestrating skill bullet, branch-reviewer check, and the `kb.mjs` co-change lines if the drift holds them) and diff the remaining drift.

items.title: Switch this repository to pnpm and set the workspace up like tag-pilot
body: Owner ruling of 2026-09-01 (docs/design.md §5.7): use pnpm only, never npm or npx.

Scope: exact `node` and `pnpm` pins in `mise.toml` written by `mise use`; `pnpm-lock.yaml` replaces `package-lock.json`; `pnpm-workspace.yaml` for the pnpm settings; the mise tasks `setup`, `test`, `lint`, and `audit` as in tag-pilot; README, knowledge entries, and the development commands name pnpm. `template/` stays dependency-free.
The batch 2 spec fixes the file list and settles the commitlint commit-msg hook.

items.title: Capture the render child's stderr in init instead of inheriting it
body: `install` in `bin/houserules.mjs` spawns `tools/kb.mjs render` with an inherited stderr, so the init test on broken project data prints one usage-error line into the suite output (tests/init.test.mjs, 'lets a render failure on broken project data propagate as a real error').
Fix: spawn with `stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']` and put the child's stderr into the thrown error; the test asserts the message and the suite output stays silent.
Source: task 3 re-review and the batch 2 branch review (2026-09-01).

items.title: Enforce the commit body line limit in the commits check
body: The `commits` check of `tools/kb.sh audit` tests the subject pattern and `body_absent` only; two controller commits with 190- and 227-character body lines passed the batch 2 audits as '9 commits checked'. Only the commit-msg hook catches it, for commits made after it was installed.

Fix: add the optional key `body_line_max` (integer, minimum 1) to `$defs.check` in `knowledge/schema.json` and `template/knowledge/schema.json`; in the `commits` runner of `template/tools/kb.mjs`, fail a commit with a body line longer than the limit; regression tests for 100 and 101 characters and a `checkShape` case; `update --dir .`.

Ruled 2026-09-01 (docs/design.md §5.8): the same task sets `body_line_max: 100` on `process.conventional-commits` in `knowledge/process.json` and `template/knowledge/process.json`. Source: batch 2 branch review, violated_rules.

items.title: Agent template and deliverables refinements from the batch 2 retrospective
body: Deliverables schema (`template/.claude/schemas/deliverables.json` and the root copy): add an optional integer `exit` to `$defs.run`; the implementer template's Report section names it for every run whose exit code is evidence, and `output` stays verbatim (batch 2: exit codes were written into `output` as prose).

Implementer template `coverage`: 'one measure per target whenever the project has a coverage gate and the full suite ran, so the batch keeps a baseline; null only when the suite did not run' (batch 2 task 1 left it null and a fix round repaired it).

Orchestrating skill, dispatch protocol: a brief names no version number for a tool, action, or package (security-hygiene.exact-pins); it names the verification the implementer runs and shows placeholders such as `jdx/mise-action@<current major>` (batch 2 task 1 brief carried a stale `@v2`).
Source: batch 2 branch review, template_defects 2-4.

items.title: Audit report-field checks over a workspace of task reports
body: A branch has no single report, so the four report-field rows (deliverables-json, knowledge-first, dependency-vetting, verify-current-docs) come back `skipped` from `tools/kb.sh audit` and the branch reviewer judges them by hand from the task reports.

Fix: accept `--report` more than once, or add `--workspace <dir>` that reads every `task-*-report.json`; a report-field check passes when every report whose changed files trigger it sets the field, and names the offending report otherwise. Source: batch 2 branch review, template_defects 5.

items.title: Diff the audit range from the merge base
body: `changedFiles` in `template/tools/kb.mjs` diffs `base..head`, so the pull-request audit (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) sees unrelated files when main moves after the branch was cut. Inherited from tag-pilot's knowledge.yml.

Fix: `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR --merge-base <base> <head>` for the files, `git log <base>..<head>` for the commits; a test with a moved base. Source: batch 2 branch review, recommendations.

items.title: Report an unreadable .houserules.json as a usage error
body: `install` parses the stamp with raw `JSON.parse(readFileSync(markerPath))`; an unreadable `.houserules.json` escapes as a SyntaxError stack trace. `tests/init.test.mjs` (the test "propagates an unreadable marker, which is a defect and not a usage error") pins the current behavior until this item.

Fix: reuse `readJson` from `template/tools/lib/json-store.mjs` (it raises `UsageError` with `<path>: invalid JSON (...)`; the bin already imports from that module) and rewrite the pinning test the way HR-005 rewrote its predecessor.
Source: batch 3 task 1 review (2026-09-01); the branch review filed the missing item as its critical finding.

items.title: Carry the git stderr in the no-merge-base usage error
body: `gitDiff` in `template/tools/kb.mjs` reports every `git diff` failure as `no merge base between "<base>" and "<head>"` and discards the child stderr, so a different failure (a missing object in a shallow clone, repository corruption) is mislabeled and its diagnostic lost.
Fix: pipe the child stderr and include it in the `UsageError`, or use the no-merge-base text only when the stderr indicates it; sync the root copy; one test.
Deferred from batch 3 with the branch review’s reason: `rev` pre-validates both refs, so the remaining failure modes are exotic. Source: batch 3 branch review, minor 2 (2026-09-01).

items.title: Dispatch-protocol bullets: a brief carries the spec, a dispatch carries changed templates
body: Two additions to the orchestrating skill’s dispatch protocol (`template/.claude/skills/orchestrating/SKILL.md`, kit-owned, then `update --dir .`): a brief names every test and gate its spec task lists, verbatim or by pointer (batch 3 task 3’s brief dropped the seed-checkBase test and the gap cost a review round); when a batch edits an agent template, the dispatch message carries the changed instruction verbatim, because templates load at session start (batch 3’s branch review ran on the pre-branch template).
Consider seeding `process.brief-carries-the-spec` (added to the root knowledge at the batch 3 close) into `template/knowledge/process.json` in the same task.
Source: batch 3 branch review, template_defects 1 and 3 (2026-09-01).

items.title: A migration skill: move a pre-existing codebase’s knowledge into the houserules style
body: Owner request of 2026-09-01: when houserules is installed into a codebase that already has knowledge (CLAUDE.md prose, docs, wikis, comments, ad-hoc rules files), a skill in the payload explains how to migrate it: inventory the sources, split rule/invariant/gotcha/procedure/decision/history, write entries per the schema (summary is the rule, ≤160; body why/how/exceptions; source with date and by; verify paths; check where deterministic), extend areas, park the leftovers, delete the migrated originals, and gate with tools/kb.sh check plus render.

Shape to design in the batch spec: a kit-owned skill (template/.claude/skills/, overwritten by update) that the README’s install-to-existing section points to; likely with a worked example and the knowledge-base.* rules by pointer.
Candidate for batch 5 with its own spec gate.

items.title: Read settings.json through readJson in the bin
body: `mergeSettings` in `bin/houserules.mjs` still parses `.claude/settings.json` by hand and wraps the failure as `not readable JSON (...)`, a second wording for the failure class the stamp path now reports as `invalid JSON` through `readJson`.

Fix: `settings = readJson(path)` and drop the catch; the existing test asserts exit 2 and the file name only. Decide the one semantic change: an unreadable (not just invalid) settings.json then propagates as a plain Error, like the stamp.
Source: batch 4 task 1 review, minor (2026-09-01); deferred out of HR-010 because of that semantics decision.

items.title: Commit-msg hook rejects trailers; ship .githooks in the payload
body: The hook runs commitlint only, so a harness-injected Co-Authored-By trailer reached a batch 4 commit and was caught by hand (task 3); security-hygiene.no-coauthor is enforced only post-hoc by the audit.

Fix: a trailer gate in .githooks/commit-msg before commitlint (grep -qiE for Co-Authored-By → one error line, exit 1). Consider shipping .githooks in the kit payload (KIT_OWNED) so consumers get the gate; this repository has no template copy of the hook today.
Source: batch 4 branch review, template_defects 1 (2026-09-02).

items.title: A structured live_run field in task reports, with a recipe check
body: Live-run evidence has no structured field, so a missing scratch recipe is findable only in prose (batch 4 task 2). Add an optional live_run array (command, output, exit) to $defs.taskReport in both deliverables schema copies; give houserules.live-run-recipe a report-field check at warn on live_run; the implementer template names the field.
Source: batch 4 branch review, template_defects 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: A mode field on tdd cycles: natural, mutation, or reconstructed
body: A tdd cycle cannot say how it was produced; batch 4 task 4 spent two report rounds wording the difference between a natural RED, a mutation proof, and a post-commit reconstruction. Add an optional mode enum (natural | mutation | reconstructed) to $defs.tddCycle in both schema copies and one implementer-template sentence: set mode when the cycle is not a natural pre-commit RED.
Source: batch 4 branch review, template_defects 3 (2026-09-02).

items.title: Co-change evidence names a record-only change plainly
body: When the then file itself matches the if glob, the co-change evidence is circular ("record.json changed with record.json"). In template/tools/kb.mjs: when the only if match is the then path, print "only <then> changed; the co-change is satisfied by definition"; otherwise exclude the then path from the listed if matches. Behavior unchanged; one test.
Source: batch 4 branch review, template_defects 4 (2026-09-02).

items.title: Area glob matching misses dot-segments under **
body: node:path matchesGlob excludes dot-segments under **: matchesGlob('template/.claude/skills/migrating-knowledge/SKILL.md', 'template/**') returns false (verified live in the batch 5 branch review). Every batch 5 audit ran without the template area: houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins dropped out of the audit package, and the rules loader never serves .claude/rules/template.md for template/.claude/** files.

Fix in template/tools/kb.mjs areaFiles (matchesGlob, ~line 106): wrap matchesGlob with a dot-inclusive variant, or a small globToRegExp with dot semantics. RED first: areasFor(['template/.claude/agents/implementer.md'], areas) must include 'template'. The fix ships in the payload; target repositories inherit it via update.
Source: batch 5 branch review, template_defects 1 (2026-09-02).

items.title: mergeSettings crashes on valid non-object JSON in settings.json
body: A .claude/settings.json containing null, a string, or a number passes readJson and then crashes with a plain TypeError stack at settings.hooks ??= {}. Pre-existing behavior, not regressed by batch 5 task 2.
Cover it with the CLI's one-line UsageError convention. RED first: a scratch settings.json containing null.
Source: batch 5 branch review, recommendation 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: A verdict.text field for re-review prose; open lists only prior findings
body: verdict.open is a bare textList; batch 5 task-1-review-r1.json used it for a status sentence plus restatements of both new_breakage items, so state 'findings-remain' read as prior findings open when all eight were addressed and only new breakage remained.

Add an optional verdict.text for prose to $defs.reReview in .claude/schemas/deliverables.json (root and template). State in task-reviewer.md that open lists only prior findings still unaddressed and that new breakage lives only in new_breakage.
Changing task-reviewer.md triggers process.evals-rerun: re-run every scenario and append the run set to .claude/evals/record.json.
Source: batch 5 branch review, template_defects 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: The stamp read crashes on a non-object .houserules.json
body: install reads the marker with 'existsSync(markerPath) ? readJson(markerPath) : { idPrefix: prefix }' and then touches marker.idPrefix; a .houserules.json holding null (or a string, a number, a boolean, an array) passes readJson and crashes with a raw stack at bin/houserules.mjs:185. Verified live at batch 6 HEAD 8175928: first init exit 0, 'printf null > .houserules.json', second init exit 1 with the stack.
Fix as HR-020's sibling: reject a non-object marker with the one-line UsageError convention ('<path>: not a JSON object'), RED first; the existing HR-010 stamp tests stay green.
Source: batch 6 task 3 review, minor 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: Re-review dispatches carry the round-0 block; audits refuse a missing --ids
body: The batch 6 task 1 round-1 re-review dispatch omitted the Backlog: line and the --ids list, so task-1-audit-r1.json ran a narrowed package (27 rows; houserules.live-run-recipe and houserules.node-under-mise dropped). The reviewer caught it; round 2 was dispatched correctly, but nothing forces the block.

Fix: the orchestrating skill's re-review dispatch bullet requires the identical Knowledge:/Backlog:/--ids block as the round-0 dispatch; the task-reviewer template refuses to run an audit without --ids when the task's id list is non-empty.
Changing task-reviewer.md triggers process.evals-rerun: re-run every scenario and append the run set to .claude/evals/record.json.
Source: batch 6 branch review, template_defects 1 (2026-09-02).

items.title: Stamp an empty-range audit as vacuous
body: An audit with base == head (batch 6 task 1's report-only round 2) succeeds with vacuous deterministic rows ('0 commits checked', '0 files checked', 'not triggered') that read as positive evidence; the round-2 reviewer had to annotate them as vacuous by hand.
Fix in template/tools/kb.mjs: when the range holds no commits, set "empty_range": true in the audit summary and prefix the deterministic evidence strings with 'empty range:'. RED first.
Source: batch 6 branch review, template_defects 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: Pin the two SEED_ONCE deliverables schema copies in sync
body: tests/dogfood.test.mjs pins every KIT_OWNED root copy byte-for-byte, but .claude/schemas/deliverables.json is SEED_ONCE: update never writes it, and its root and template copies are hand-synced. They differ only in the backlogId pattern (HR- vs WI-) by design.
Batch 7 hand-synced four new fields across both copies on manual diligence alone. Add a test that compares the copies modulo the known backlogId pattern difference, so a drift fails the suite.
Source: batch 7 task 3 review, controller note (2026-09-02).

items.title: The audit package admits area-matched entries that carry a check
body: The package builder (template/tools/kb.mjs:709) admits only standing entries and area-matched rule/invariant kinds, so the report-field check on houserules.live-run-recipe (kind procedure, area cli) never joins a range-derived package: the batch 7 branch audit carried no live_run row though the plan promised it. Task audits carried it only via --ids.

Fix: admit any area-matched entry that carries a check (e.g. e.check && areas.includes(e.area)), RED first with a regression test that a checked procedure joins the package; template first, root synced. Damage is minor today because the schema makes live_run required, which fails validate harder than the warn row.

Deferred out of batch 7 by the controller: audit-machinery semantics deserve full review rounds, not a post-branch-review patch. Source: batch 7 branch review, minor 1 + template_defects 1 (2026-09-02).

items.title: The stamp guard validates idPrefix as a string
body: readJsonObject accepts any plain object, so a .houserules.json holding an idPrefix that is a number passes the guard and the number flows into id generation. Owner-candidate: decide whether the stamp is fully validated or the object guard suffices.
Source: batch 7 task 1 review, reviewer note (2026-09-02).

items.title: install validates the stamp before writing kit-owned files
body: install rewrites every KIT_OWNED file before it reads the stamp, so a corrupt .houserules.json exits 2 with the target already updated. Pre-existing since batch 4; same order as the invalid-JSON path. Owner-candidate: decide whether the stamp read moves ahead of the writes.
Source: batch 7 task 1 review, reviewer note (2026-09-02).

items.title: The dependency-add eval query names its payload collision
body: The query names the project's tooling package, which collides with houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins when run in this repository, forcing a deviation disclosure every run; the judge cannot tell a designed trap from an accidental ambiguity.
Fix: name the repository's own devDependencies in the query, or add the collision to expected_behavior as an explicit judged criterion. Changing a scenario triggers process.evals-rerun.
Source: batch 7 branch review, template_defects 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: implementer.md's Report section lists one field per line
body: After live_run and mode landed, the Report field list is one long single sentence; each contract change re-inflates it and makes template diffs hard to review. Restructure as one line per field, wording unchanged.
Changing implementer.md triggers process.evals-rerun; schedule with the next template batch.
Source: batch 7 branch review, template_defects 4 (2026-09-02).

items.title: One idPrefix predicate serves the flag and the stamp
body: install validates the --id-prefix flag with /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{0,7}$/ but the stamp guard (HR-027) accepts any non-empty string, so a hand-edited .houserules.json can carry a prefix init would refuse (' ', 'wi', 'TOOLONGPREFIX') and the next line writes it back. Two validators for one concept in one function.

RULED by the owner 2026-09-02: unify on the flag's regex (/^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{0,7}$/) as one shared predicate with one message, in the flag check and the stamp guard both. RED first; the HR-027 tests move to the shared message where applicable.
Source: batch 8 task 3 review, minor 4 (2026-09-02).

items.title: Pin the seeded eval scenario copies to their template sources
body: No gate pins .claude/evals/{dependency-add,docs-edit,seeded-violations}.json to their template/.claude/evals/ sources: dogfood parity covers KIT_OWNED only, and HR-025's batch 8 pin covers the deliverables schema pair. Batch 8 T5 made the dependency-add pair carry a judged criterion that must not drift; a one-sided edit would ship a seeded scenario that grades differently from the one this repository runs on itself.
Add a sync test beside the deliverables-schema pin for the three scenario copies. Exclude record.json: the root copy holds run sets and the template copy ships empty, so they differ by design.
Source: batch 8 task 5 review, minor 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: implementer.md's tdd bullet carries the timing-key example inline
body: Ruling 18's first enforcement cost a Critical, a sanctioned amend, and a fix round: the batch 8 task 4 implementer re-ran the RED against checked-out pre-fix code after the fix existed and read the natural label as a statement about code state, not chronology.

Add the decisive example inline to the template's tdd bullet: a RED re-captured against pre-fix code after the fix exists is reconstructed; natural is chronology, not code state. Changing implementer.md triggers process.evals-rerun; schedule with the next template batch.
Source: batch 8 branch review, template_defects 2 (2026-09-02).

items.title: The dispatch protocol states that --ids IS the Knowledge list
body: Task-brief boilerplate carries a hand-filled --ids line nothing pins to the dispatch's Knowledge list; the batch 8 task 5 brief shipped the T3/T4 cli ids into a data-only task and only the implementer's cross-check caught it. The retrieval protocol implies the equality but never states it.

State it in the orchestrating skill's dispatch section and in the retrieval protocol text in template/tools/kb.mjs: the audit --ids value IS the dispatch's Knowledge list, generated from it, never typed separately. Add one skill sentence requiring a ledger line for every guard-caught controller slip (batch 8 branch review, template_defects 3). The kb.mjs retrieval-protocol change needs a scenario re-run per process.evals-rerun's body; schedule with HR-033.
Source: batch 8 branch review, template_defects 1 and 3 (2026-09-02).

items.title: The test suite cleans its mkdtemp scratch directories
body: tests/ has 21 mkdtempSync call sites across seven files and none removes its directory; every pnpm test run adds a full seeded project tree per init target. At the batch 9 task 2 review /tmp held 1714 orphaned houserules-target-* directories plus 89 kb-* and 15 ws-*, and a transient inode exhaustion had already broken one suite attempt (disclosed in the task 2 report).

Fix: give the mkdtemp sites cleanup — onTestFinished/afterEach with rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }), or one fixture helper that mints and registers scratch dirs. Behavior of the tests unchanged; the suite leaves /tmp as it found it.
Source: batch 9 task 2 review, controller escalation resolved (2026-09-03).

Rider (batch 9 branch review): land the knowledge entry houserules.tests-clean-scratch-dirs with the retrofit, so the rule has a loading path the moment the call sites are fixed. Summary: 'Every test that mints a scratch directory registers its removal at the mkdtemp site: onTestFinished/afterEach with rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }), or the shared fixture helper.' Area tests; the body names the 1714-orphan census and states the suite leaves /tmp as it found it.

items.title: The report status field ties to a non-empty concerns list
body: implementer.md defines DONE_WITH_CONCERNS only for the final chat message; nothing ties the report's status field to a non-empty concerns list. Batch 9 produced two reports whose file says DONE while the agent's answer and the ledger say DONE_WITH_CONCERNS (task 3; the dependency-add eval scenario). The report file is the artifact of record, so the divergence leaves the returned status ambiguous.

Fix: one sentence at the status bullet — set status to DONE_WITH_CONCERNS whenever concerns is non-empty; the answer message repeats the report's status verbatim. Changing implementer.md triggers process.evals-rerun.
Source: batch 9 branch review, template_defects 1 (2026-09-03).

items.title: The ledger bullet covers every controller slip, gate-caught or not
body: The orchestrating skill's ledger bullet binds only slips that a gate or && chain catches; a slip caught by inspection carries no logging duty. The gap showed the day the sentence shipped: the record-commit indent amend, caught by re-reading the diff stat and not by a gate, went unlogged, and a second formatting slip in the batch 9 finish repeated the class.

Fix: widen the bullet to every controller slip that forces a re-run, an amend, or a correction — gate-caught or not — logged when it happens. Skill-only change; no scenario covers the orchestrating skill, so no re-run is due.
Source: batch 9 branch review, template_defects 2 (2026-09-03).

items.title: Adopters can update their vendored kit when houserules releases changes
body: A project that adopted the kit has no defined path to newer kit versions. init and update stamp the running CLI's version into .houserules.json (bin/houserules.mjs writes { version, idPrefix }), but nothing reads the stamp back for comparison: an adopter learns of a new release nowhere, and no doc states the flow (bump the houserules dependency, run update, review the diff).

Shape: the CLI reports stamped-versus-running drift (update prints what version it upgrades from and to; files or a status command surfaces it read-only); README documents the adopter flow end to end. Details to the batch spec when scheduled.
Source: owner, 2026-09-03 (docs/design.md §5.19). Pairs with HR-039 — the release machinery makes a new version a real, announced event.

items.title: Semver releases via release-please with an alpha pre-release
body: RULED by the owner 2026-09-03 (docs/design.md §5.19): versioning is semver; changelogs are generated from the conventional commits; the tool is release-please; the first release is a pre-release under the alpha dist-tag; the GitHub upstream is created right after the alpha-state tasks are done. Until the upstream exists, decision 3's constraint stands: no remote, no gh repo create, no npm publish.

Shape: local groundwork can land before the upstream (release-please config and manifest, prerelease alpha versioning strategy, the release-type choice for a single-package pnpm repo, CHANGELOG bootstrap); the automation itself runs on GitHub and activates when the upstream is created. Publishing to npm under the alpha dist-tag follows as the first release.

RULED by the owner 2026-09-03 (batch 11 gate): alpha state = HR-040 + HR-038 + this item's local groundwork, gated as batch 11; completing that batch constitutes alpha state, and the upstream creation follows immediately.
Source: owner, 2026-09-03; release-please chosen over git-cliff and changesets at the ruling.

items.title: One evals rerun pays the live_run capture form and the collision-line reword
body: Batch 10 produced three evidence-capture findings of one class (stderr redirected after the target, a command with no per-command capture, a `; cat` tail owning the recorded exit) and one undecidable eval line: dependency-add expected_behavior[1] presumes a separate dependency-free payload manifest, so a single-manifest repository passes it only by judgment — the fifth record notes the call verbatim.

Fix, one batch, one evals rerun for both: (a) the implementer.md live_run bullet states the canonical capture form — one command per entry, captured as `<command> > <file> 2>&1`, the recorded exit is that command's own, no `;` or `|` tails; (b) dependency-add expected_behavior[1] in both scenario copies rewords to two decidable outcomes — with a payload manifest present, place the dependency outside it and disclose the collision in concerns; with the root manifest as the only manifest, keep the payload import-free and state the placement reasoning in the report.
Source: batch 10 branch review, template_defects 1 and 2 (2026-09-03).

items.title: validate rejects a terminal-status report with a null self_audit
body: A task report with status DONE or DONE_WITH_CONCERNS and self_audit null passes tools/kb.sh validate. Batch 11 task 3's implementer was interrupted mid-finalization by a session restart; the on-disk report looked schema-complete and only the controller's null probe caught the gap.

Fix: validate fails when a task-report's status is terminal and self_audit is null. The retrieval protocol's write-then-fill flow keeps working: the pre-fill report carries no terminal claim the validator trusts. Template tools/kb.mjs + root sync; deliverables schema unchanged unless the check fits there better.

Extension (batch 12 branch review, template_defects 2): the same validate change also rejects a task-report whose self_audit.summary.skipped is greater than 0, naming the --report flag in the message — a fix-round audit recorded without --report validated cleanly and cost a follow-up round.
Source: batch 11 branch review, template_defects 1 (2026-09-03); batch 12 branch review, template_defects 2 (2026-09-03).

items.title: The dependency-vetting check triggers on workflow action references
body: The security-hygiene.dependency-vetting deterministic trigger keys on package manifests only, so a diff adding googleapis/release-please-action@v5.0.0 — third-party code running with contents:write — showed 'not triggered' and the batch 11 T3 reviewer had to file the missing vetting record by hand.

Fix: extend the trigger — a diff that adds or changes a `uses:` reference under .github/workflows/ requires dependency_vetting with the workflow file in manifests and the action reference in dependencies. Requires the owner's ruling first: the check lives on a STANDING entry (both knowledge copies) and the runner change lives in crates/houserules/src/rules/audit.rs's `run_check` (batch 20 T3 retired template/tools/kb.mjs, the runner's pre-rewrite home).
Source: batch 11 branch review, violated_rules 2 and template_defects 2 (2026-09-03). Standing-entry change: OWNER RULING PENDING, listed in the batch 11 report.

items.title: Reviewer prescriptions state the invariant plus the observed instance
body: Batch 11 T2 r0's prescription named only the observed instance ('present but not a string raises UsageError'), so the empty-string case survived one fix round; the r1 ruling charged the residual scope to the prescription's literal wording, not the implementer.

Fix: one sentence in .claude/agents/task-reviewer.md's findings guidance — state each fix as the invariant to hold plus the observed instance, so an implementer who fixes to the letter also fixes the intent. Changing task-reviewer.md triggers process.evals-rerun; schedule with the next template batch.
Source: batch 11 branch review, template_defects 3 (2026-09-03).

items.title: The release version bump breaks CI: stale dogfood stamp and a pre-release-blind test regex
body: The 0.2.0-alpha release commit turned main red: tests/dogfood.test.mjs expects the repo stamp to equal the running VERSION, but .houserules.json still says 0.1.0 (nobody ran update after the bump); tests/init.test.mjs asserts the stamped version matches /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/, which rejects every pre-release version although the owner ruled pre-release alpha versions the norm (design.md 5.19).

Fix: run node bin/houserules.mjs update --dir . so the stamp follows the bump (the drift line prints kit 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0-alpha, its first production use) and commit the restamp; widen the init test regex to accept a semver pre-release suffix. Consider: every future release PR merge needs the restamp — either document it in the release runbook or make CI tolerant of the one-commit lag; decide in the spec.
Source: first release cycle, CI runs 33789904843 and 33782255156 (2026-09-03).

items.title: A proper README and the open-source repository files
body: Owner request 2026-09-03 (after the alpha release went public): write a proper README and add all necessary files and settings for an open-source repository.

Shape: the README presents the kit to a first-time visitor (what it is, why, install, quick start, the ownership model, the agent workflow, badges once CI is public); CONTRIBUTING.md carries the development workflow (mise/pnpm setup, the batch process, conventional commits, the no-trailer rule); SECURITY.md, a code of conduct, issue and PR templates under .github/; repository settings (description, topics); LICENSE already exists (MIT). Details to the batch spec when scheduled.
Source: owner, 2026-09-03; scheduled after the HR-044 hotfix per the owner's instruction.

items.title: The finishing-a-feature skill carries the release-please restamp step
body: The post-release restamp procedure loads for docs/runbook.md (area docs), but the agent doing a release merge edits .houserules.json and package.json, which sit in the global area — tools/kb.sh for on those paths does not surface the step, and the skill that drives every merge says nothing about release-please PRs. That is exactly how HR-044 happened.

Fix per the batch 12 branch review's recommendation (skill, not standing — a rare-event procedure as a standing rule would dilute the list every agent loads): add one step to template/.claude/skills/finishing-a-feature/SKILL.md — after merging a release-please PR, run mise exec -- node bin/houserules.mjs update --dir ., commit chore(release): restamp the kit version, push (houserules.post-release-restamp, docs/runbook.md). Root sync via update --dir .; no scenario covers the skill, so no evals rerun.
Source: batch 12 branch review, template_defects 1 (2026-09-03).

items.title: Rewrite the toolchain as one static binary (Tier 2)
body: RULED by the owner 2026-09-03: go straight to Tier 2 — no Tier 0 (version-manager-provided Node) and no Tier 1 (bundled-JS binaries) interim steps. The kit becomes runs-anywhere: one compiled, statically linked houserules binary replaces the Node toolchain end to end.

Scope: rewrite bin/houserules.mjs, template/tools/kb.mjs, and template/tools/backlog.mjs in RUST (RULED 2026-09-04, design.md 5.21); the vendored tools/kb.sh and tools/backlog.sh become thin POSIX shims that exec the houserules binary on PATH; every existing behavior carries over under the current suite's contracts (init/update, KIT_OWNED sync and the stamp with its drift line, render, check, audit, validate, the backlog commands). The payload invariant houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins redefines to one static binary plus POSIX shell — a docs/design.md amendment and an owner ruling at spec time.

Migration: the JS suite pins today's behavior; port tests alongside the rewrite; parity gates (byte-identical render output, identical audit JSON on the same range) hold before the JS path retires. Multi-batch work; the spec decides the slicing.
Source: owner, 2026-09-03 (Tier 2 direct, superseding the tiered distribution proposal).

COMPLETE 2026-09-08, batch 20 (Tier 2 closes): phase 3 put the payload in the binary and self-flipped the repository (batch 18, main a20a179); phase 4 wired the release channels (batch 19, main 6a79ace); phase 5 retired everything JS -- bin/houserules.mjs, the frozen corpus and make-corpus, the vitest layer, package.json/pnpm/node, and the shipped-but-inert payload engines -- with the parity contract re-baselined as Rust-generated goldens and a permanent residue gate in mise run lint. Acceptance per spec 2026-09-07-batch-20-phase5.md section 10: the tree builds, tests, lints, and gates through cargo and the binary alone with no package.json; a fresh init seeds zero JS; the residue gate runs zero-unexpected (.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-07-batch-20/acceptance-run.txt).

items.title: Binary delivery channels for the rewritten kit (Tier 2)
body: RULED with HR-047: distribution targets the compiled binary, not npm-first. Deliverables: per-platform release binaries (linux and macOS on x64 and arm64, Windows) built and attached by CI at each release-please release, with checksums and a signing/notarization decision for macOS; mise via the ubi backend; an asdf plugin consuming the release binaries; a Homebrew tap; Scoop or winget; a curl-to-sh installer. npm RETIRES (RULED 2026-09-04, design.md 5.22): binary-only distribution; a wrapper package stays purely additive later if demand appears.

Prerequisite RULED 2026-09-04 (design.md 5.20): plain v<version>. include-component-in-tag goes false at the next config-touching task; the alias tag v0.2.0-alpha already points at the existing release commit, so every channel builds on the v* grammar from the first release.

External acts (the plugin repository, registry PRs, the tap) are owner-attended per the decision 3 precedent. Blocked by HR-047 producing the binary; the spec may land the tag-format ruling and the CI scaffolding earlier.
Source: owner, 2026-09-03 (Tier 2 direct, no Tier 0 or Tier 1 channels).

items.title: The README's pinned install tag follows each release
body: README.md pins the install form to houserules-v0.2.0-alpha in three places (the r0 unpinned form was the worse defect); nothing in the release flow updates them, so the next release leaves the README installing an old kit — a knowledge-base.state-only-the-source decay at the first post-merge release.

Fix: wire the pins into the release flow — release-please extra-files annotations if they support the shape, else one line in the restamp step of docs/runbook.md and the finishing-a-feature skill (update the README pins with the restamp commit). Decide the mechanism in the batch spec. Interlock: HR-048's tag-format ruling may rename the tag grammar these pins use — schedule together or after it.

Batch 19 T2: measured and wired. release-please v17.11.2's Generic updater treats a bare string in `extra-files` as annotation-scanned text, verified against its own source (src/updaters/generic.ts at the pinned tag) and the pinned config schema. Wired six pin lines in README.md (the shell-installer URL, the five direct-download archive links) via x-release-please-start-version/-end blocks placed outside the runnable code fences, plus the seeded template/.github/workflows/knowledge.yml's own install-step pin via one inline x-release-please-version marker -- seven lines total across the two files, each proven with a RED (pre-fix content, no markers, replacement count assert-fails) and GREEN (shipped content, exact count) reproduction of the updater's own regex logic. STAYS OPEN: the mechanism is wired, not yet verified live -- closes only once a real release-please release actually replaces these pins and a fresh capture confirms the new pin resolves (docs/specs/2026-09-06-batch-19-phase4.md §7's step two).
Source: batch 13 branch review, issue 2 (2026-09-03).

items.title: One evals rerun pays the verbatim-output rule and the findings-list check
body: Two agent-template defects from the batch 13 branch review pair for one evals rerun: (a) implementer.md's live_run guidance gains one sentence — output carries the command's stdout/stderr verbatim and nothing else; the exit field alone carries the exit status (T2's captures appended a synthetic exit=0 line inside output); (b) task-reviewer.md's re-review checklist gains one sentence — confirm the fix round's findings list matches the review's findings one for one before ruling all-addressed (T2's fix_rounds[0] listed four of five, caught only in prose).

Riding free (skill-only, no rerun): the orchestrating skill's rebuild guidance gains a step — on a mid-batch branch rebuild, write the old-to-new sha map to its own workspace file, cite it in the batch report, never edit closed-task deliverables (the batch 13 rebuild left the map ledger-only until the branch review flagged it).
Source: batch 13 branch review, template_defects 1-3 (2026-09-03).

items.title: One evals rerun pays the nested-audit gate and the verbatim-clause lift
body: Two template defects from the batch 14 branch review pair for the next template-touching batch: (a) the hardened validate inspects only the top-level self_audit, so a fix-round audit recorded without --report — the batch 12 shape — still validates; it recurred inside batch 14 itself (T1 fix round 0, skipped 3) and only the task reviewer caught it. Decide in the spec: extend checkTaskReportAudit to scan fix_rounds[].tests[].output for an audit summary carrying a nonzero skipped, or keep it judged by adding the check to the task-reviewer's numbered list. (b) implementer.md's verbatim-output invariant governs tests, live_run, and fix_rounds[].tests but sits inside live_run's parenthetical — lift it onto its own line above the field list, wording unchanged.

Optional rider if the owner wants it: recompress task-reviewer.md item 6 to one sentence (it grew a second, disposition sentence in the batch 14 fix round; the two-sentence form is correct, so this is polish only).
Source: batch 14 branch review, template_defects 1-2 and recommendation 1 (2026-09-04).

items.title: Write and gate the Tier-2 rewrite spec
body: Batch 15 delivers the spec for the owner-ruled Tier-2 rewrite (HR-047: one static binary replaces bin/houserules.mjs and the vendored kb/backlog tools; HR-048: binary delivery channels). The build itself spans later batches; HR-047/048 stay open through the spec.

The spec gate carries the owner rulings, one at a time: the release tag format (plain v<version> against houserules-v<version> — the HR-048 prerequisite, also unblocking HR-049); the implementation language (Go against Rust); the payload-contract redefinition for docs/design.md (one static binary + POSIX shell replaces Node-builtins-only); the role npm keeps after the rewrite; the parity gates (byte-identical render, identical audit JSON) and the phasing.
Source: owner gate 2026-09-04 (batch 15: begin the Tier-2 spec).

items.title: Modular installs: adopters choose the feature set
body: Owner intent recorded at the Tier-2 CLI-surface ruling (2026-09-04): houserules becomes modular — an adopter can install only backlog management, or rules management without the backlog, or the full kit. This is WHY the flat command surface keeps per-module checks (check-knowledge, check-backlog) and the Rust crate separates rules, backlog, and install modules.

Shape: a feature/selection mechanism in init (and update honoring it) that installs a subset of the payload — the seeded files, generated artifacts, skills, and checks scoped to the chosen modules; the stamp records the selection. Details to the batch spec when gated, AFTER the Tier-2 port completes (the port ships everything; the crate boundaries prepare the split).
Source: owner, 2026-09-04, at the batch 15 CLI-surface ruling; the Tier-2 spec's architecture section carries the boundary design.

items.title: Tier-2 phase 1: the frozen corpus and the Rust scaffold
body: Phase 1 of the approved Tier-2 spec (docs/specs/2026-09-04-batch-15-tier2-spec.md §5.1), under HR-047: the cargo workspace with the rules/backlog/install module boundaries, the CI matrix, the frozen fixture corpus generated by the JS implementation at the migration base, and `render` plus `check-knowledge` in Rust behind the byte-parity gate. Their tests land as cargo tests from day one; the glob union matcher is the first parity target. The cross-compilation spike (cargo-dist against cross/zig) settles here for phase 4.
Source: owner gate 2026-09-04 (batch 16: phase 1).

items.title: Default starter rule set: docs and code-quality style adopters begin with
body: Owner intent (2026-09-04): adopters should start with a curated default set of rules — docs style and code-quality style in tag-pilot's vein — instead of a near-empty seed. Today template/knowledge/ ships 36 entries that are process-heavy (23 process entries) while quality carries 2 and writing-style 3; no docs-style or language-agnostic code-quality starter content exists.

Shape: curate a default entry set for the quality and writing-style topics (and a docs area if warranted), modeled on the tag-pilot checkout's rules as a READ-ONLY reference (houserules.tag-pilot-is-read-only). Content work, independent of the Tier-2 binary; interacts with HR-053 (a starter set is what a modular rules-only install would seed). Curation choices and any new areas go to the batch spec when gated.
Source: owner, 2026-09-04, mid batch 16.

items.title: Pin the bare `houserules` invocation behavior
body: Batch 16 branch review, issue 4: bare `houserules` with no subcommand exits 0 silently (clap Command is Option, None maps to SUCCESS) — untested, undocumented, and new flat-surface behavior outside the parity gates; tools/kb.sh with no command prints usage and fails.

Fix in phase 2 when the next subcommands land, per the reviewer's own timing: set clap's arg_required_else_help(true), or pin the current behavior with a test and a doc comment stating why. Deferred because the choice interacts with the phase-2 command surface.
Source: batch 16 branch review, 2026-09-04.

items.title: Capture-file citations for oversized report evidence
body: Batch 16 branch review, template defect 1: task-4-report.json reached 583KB because all 41 tdd entries embed verbatim RED/GREEN inline; reviewers re-ran cycles anyway, and T5's fix round already invented the better shape (bulk evidence in named workspace files, byte-prefix-matching inline excerpts).

Change: let a tdd or live_run entry cite a workspace capture file by path for output beyond a stated size, keeping the first lines plus exit inline; standardize the t5-evidence/ convention in .claude/schemas/deliverables.json and both agent templates. Deferred from batch 16 because template changes trigger process.evals-rerun and the batch was already closing.
Source: batch 16 branch review retrospective, 2026-09-04.

items.title: kb audit: an explicit empty-range mode
body: Batch 16 branch review, template defect 2: T5's three empty-range audits (research task, no diff) produced three byte-identical near-vacuous files — every deterministic row passes trivially and none speaks to the actual deliverable; the schema still demands self_audit, so the ritual ran three times for no signal.

Change: give audit an explicit empty-range mode that says so in one summary row (it already emits empty_range: true), and let a research task's report point its evidence rows at the workspace doc instead of the diff. Ships in template/tools until the Tier-2 port owns audit (phase 2), then carries into the Rust audit.
Source: batch 16 branch review retrospective, 2026-09-04.

items.title: Tier-2 phase 2: audit, validate, stats, and the backlog commands in Rust
body: Phase 2 of the approved Tier-2 spec (docs/specs/2026-09-04-batch-15-tier2-spec.md §5.2), under HR-047: the deterministic check runners and serde schema models — `audit` (field-identical JSON against the corpus), `validate`, `stats`, and the backlog commands (`list`, `get`, `set`, `batch`, `check-backlog`) — with their vitest cases ported per the coverage-ratchet pattern (houserules.vitest-coverage-floor-tracks-the-rust-port) and per-surface live behavioral gates.

Carries from batch 16: wire glob_match/area_files/areas_for into audit and for, dropping the #[allow(dead_code)] attributes in the same commit; HR-056's bare-invocation pin; freeze the skipped>0 validate message the T4 r1 re-review parked; the knowledge read commands (get, for, index, topics, standing) land here or the plan states where — the spec's phasing leaves them unassigned and the phase-3 reference rewrite needs every command shipped.

Carries from T1 (fix round 1, review issue 6): T1 landed four wholly-dormant model files, each carrying a file-level #![allow(dead_code)] (crates/houserules/src/backlog/model.rs, crates/houserules/src/json_shape.rs, crates/houserules/src/rules/deliverables.rs, crates/houserules/src/rules/check_shape.rs) — the same obligation the batch-16 carry above records, at file scope instead of per-item because every item in each file was dormant alike. Each file-level allow narrows to only the items still dead in the same commit that wires that file's first consumer (T2 for backlog/model.rs; T3 or T4 for the three rules/ files), and the allow disappears entirely once none remain.

Data-layer verdict (T2 review, per the spec §3 rule): backlog/model.rs keeps ItemStatus (the status oracle) plus anything the surface consumes; its fourteen dormant types and their pin tests are DELETED in the T2 fix round — no consumer can exist under the rule. The allow-narrowing obligation ends by deletion for a model file the port will never need. rules/deliverables.rs and check_shape.rs stay for T3’s aggregating readers, judged per the same rule at T3.

Carried from the T1 r4 re-review (reviewer-sanctioned, non-blocking): tools/check-report-claims.mjs fails open when a listed commit sha does not resolve (report an error instead; test with one unresolvable sha) and its narrative-sha check misfires after aggregation discards pre-aggregation shas (add the aggregation-window limit; consider exempting shas a sentence marks as replaced). Fix in a later phase-2 task or the batch close.

T3 data-layer verdict (per the spec §3 rule, judged as T2's own verdict above delegated): none of validate/stats/audit ends up a consumer for rules/deliverables.rs's ~30 types. validate stays on the generic schema engine (its own module doc already ruled this out at T1); stats and audit's --report/--workspace reads must stay tolerant serde_json::Value, matching the frozen JS's `?? []` fallbacks for a malformed workspace file (the rule's own worked example); and audit's own JSON output cannot reuse AuditRow/AuditRowResult at all — its judged rows carry `result: "open"`, a value .claude/schemas/deliverables.json's auditRow.result enum forbids, so the two shapes are not actually the same type despite the superficial resemblance a prior task's module doc anticipated. rules/deliverables.rs and crate::json_shape (its one remaining consumer) are DELETED with their pin tests at T3, not kept dormant a further phase — no command in the whole flat surface (spec §3) ever constructs or strictly parses a schema-exact deliverable; every schema.json/backlog.json model layer that does keep a real consumer (backlog::model's ItemStatus, check_shape.rs's CheckDef, wired into model::Entry.check and the audit engine) stays. check_shape.rs's file-level allow drops entirely.

T4 fold-ins (T3 rounds, reviewer-sanctioned deferrals): the binary-wide bare --dir divergence (JS exit 0, clap exit 2 — verified on five commands incl. render/check-knowledge; one argv-closure pass over the WHOLE flat surface at T4, extending each command’s pins); the four duplicate-value-flag pins T3’s enumeration class omitted (--head/--ids/--report/--workspace doubled; extend task-3-fix2-enumerate-argv.sh to 25 shapes); the T3 report’s one wrong exit field (fix_rounds[1].tests[0]: script exits 0, the 2 was read off its output); the T1 claims-tool carries (fail-open on unresolvable listed sha; aggregation-window Limits gap).

Residual from the T4 r2 re-review (non-blocking, reviewer-recorded): a duplicated --dir with values (--dir X --dir Y) exits 2 in the binary and 0 in the JS uniformly across all fourteen commands — the binary-own flag class argv_closure.rs governs. Cheap close at the branch review or phase 3: narrow argv_closure.rs’s duplicated-value-flags clause to flags the frozen JS also has, or add a second loop probing --dir X --dir Y across the fourteen commands.
Source: owner gate 2026-09-04 (batch 17: phase 2).

items.title: Template clauses and CI wiring from the batch 17 retrospective
body: Batch 17 branch review, template_defects: (a) .claude/agents/implementer.md gains two clauses — every audit of record, fix-diff audits included, runs WITH --report <REPORT_FILE> (two batch-17 audits ran without it, skipping the checks they appeared to cover), and the closing act is a clean node tools/check-report-claims.mjs run pasted last; (b) .claude/agents/task-reviewer.md gains the verify-by-running clause — a finding stating a measurement, reproduction, or proposed-fix behavior is run before filing (two reviewer-side errors this batch). Template changes trigger process.evals-rerun — one shared rerun.
Also homes the claims-tool CI-wiring decision (currently unwired; T1 r4 review prose): decide whether tools/check-report-claims.mjs joins a CI job or stays a closing-act tool, and record the answer.

Deferred from batch 17 for the evals cost; the paired standing-entry amendments (claims-match tool mandate, code-comments measurement clause, exact-pins Cargo extension, tests-clean-scratch-dirs check) are owner-gated at the batch 17 report and land with this item if approved.
Source: batch 17 branch review retrospective, 2026-09-05.

items.title: Port check-report-claims to a cargo bin; dev tools are Rust-native
body: Owner ruling at the batch 17 report (2026-09-05): no Node tools in the codebase - the tooling choice is Rust. Rewrite tools/check-report-claims.mjs as a bin target in the houserules crate (same five checks, the same honest Limits section, cargo-tested incl. the unresolvable-sha error and the aggregation-window limit), delete the .mjs and tests/check-report-claims.test.mjs, and update the process.claims-match-artifacts bullet to the cargo invocation in the same task.

Controller interpretation pending owner confirmation: tools/make-corpus.mjs stays as the one sanctioned interim exception - it exists to drive the FROZEN JS implementation for corpus generation and retires with the corpus at phase 5; porting it to Rust would still spawn Node, gaining nothing. Veto this and it ports too.
Schedule with HR-060 (the template clauses reference the checker) or ride batch 18.
Source: owner, 2026-09-05, batch 17 report.

items.title: Tier-2 phase 3: init/update/files, the reference rewrite, check-commit
body: Phase 3 of the approved Tier-2 spec (docs/specs/2026-09-04-batch-15-tier2-spec.md, section 5.3), under HR-047: init/update/files in Rust with the payload embedded in the binary, KIT_OWNED sync gaining the deletion capability, the stamp and drift line, the settings merge; the reference rewrite across every shipped file to the flat houserules commands; tools/kb.sh and tools/backlog.sh deleted from the payload and from installs at the next update; check-commit lands and the shipped hook probes it in place of commitlint.

The phase where the payload contract flips: the section 2 invariant amendment and the design.md section 3 ownership prose land here (re-timed from batch 16). The plan must settle: the corpus render slices get re-baselined where the sanctioned rewrite changes output; the repository itself flips its own gates, CI, docs, and mise tasks to the binary when dogfooding deletes its root shell tools; template/tools/*.mjs linger through phase 4 (the live vitest gates and corpus regeneration drive them) and retire at phase 5.
Source: owner gate 2026-09-05 (batch 18: phase 3 + HR-060/061 folded in).

items.title: Seeded knowledge.yml needs an install step before it can run
body: Batch 18 T5 fix round 1 (task-5-review.json, findings "seeded CI gate + hook" and houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins): template/.github/workflows/knowledge.yml now runs houserules check-knowledge, houserules check-backlog, and houserules audit, but no step in that job puts the houserules binary on the runner -- an adopter's houserules init seeds a PR gate whose first real step fails. The dead actions/setup-node@v7 step is dropped in the same fix round; this item tracks the missing install step itself.

Batch 19 T2: the install step now exists. A pinned cargo-dist shell-installer step (`releases/download/v<version>/houserules-installer.sh`) runs before check-knowledge/check-backlog/audit, defended against jdx/mise-action (a new marketplace-action dependency plus an inline mise.toml an adopter repo does not otherwise carry) in commit 167772b and the task report's `implemented` field. No new dependency enters this repository's own manifests; dependency_vetting there is null.

STAYS OPEN: jblossey/houserules carries one release so far (houserules-v0.2.0-alpha, 2026-09-03), and it ships zero assets; the v0.2.0-alpha tag the install step's URL actually needs has no release of its own (the releases API confirms both facts, fix round 1 t2-evidence/releases-api-listing.json). Either way the pinned URL 404s. Fix round 1 also gave the step `shell: bash`, so that 404 aborts the step itself (GitHub's documented -o pipefail) instead of surfacing two steps later as a confusing 'houserules: command not found' -- but a real CI run of the seeded step still cannot succeed until HR-048's pipeline cuts a release with assets. Closes only then, once a live run of a freshly seeded repository's PR gate proves the install step end to end (docs/specs/2026-09-06-batch-19-phase4.md §7's step two) -- the wiring is done, the verification is not.

houserules.payload-runs-on-builtins (the invariant that the SessionStart hook and the CI gates run where nothing is installed) is amended at T6 to the ruled binary+POSIX contract, and again at T2 to name this step; both amendments land against the fact each carried at the time, not silently past it.
Source: batch 18 T5 fix round 1 review, filed by the implementer per process.no-tech-debt.

items.title: README's build-from-source step follows HR-048/HR-049's real channel
body: Batch 18 T6 fix round 1 (task-6-review.json, issue 2, knowledge-base.state-only-the-source): the README's runnable blocks called a bare `houserules` binary no install path supplied. The fix round's answer is a temporary "Building the houserules binary" section (`git clone` this repository, `cargo install --path crates/houserules --bin houserules`) placed before the first bare `houserules` call, explicitly marked pending HR-048.

This item tracks retiring that section once HR-048 ships a real binary delivery channel: replace the build-from-source block with the shipped install form (the release-asset download, mise/ubi, or whichever channel HR-048 lands), and re-verify every runnable block top to bottom against it. Interlocked with HR-049 (the README's pinned install tag following each release) -- both touch the same blocks and should land together or in HR-049's wake, the same ordering HR-063 already notes for the seeded CI workflow's install step.
Blocked on HR-048; cannot land before it.

Batch 19 T2 (17a243d) performed the retirement: the build-from-source section is gone and the install blocks ship the real channels with dated PENDING control runs proving each fails for the right reason today (no release with assets). STAYS OPEN until step two: docs/runbook.md step 6's README install-block re-walk at the first release with assets closes it.
Source: batch 18 T6 fix round 1 review, issue 2 (2026-09-06).

items.title: Sync the root eval scenario copies once the shared evals rerun lands
body: Batch 18 T6 fix round 1 (task-6-review.json, issue 4, process.no-tech-debt): the three root .claude/evals/{dependency-add,docs-edit,seeded-violations}.json copies still read "tools/kb.sh validate" (T5 rewrote template/'s copies to "houserules validate"; the root copies are seed-once and update never revisits them). tests/dogfood.test.mjs pins the root/template divergence explicitly (PENDING_EVALS_RERUN_SYNC) instead of dropping the assertion, because this task's own brief bars touching .claude/evals/ directly.

items.title: release-please's tag push needs a token that starts release.yml
body: Batch 19 task 1 review, important finding: `.github/workflows/release-please.yml` invokes `googleapis/release-please-action@v5.0.0` with no `token:` input, so it tags and releases on the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`. GitHub suppresses workflow runs for events that token creates, so the tag it pushes will not start cargo-dist's generated `.github/workflows/release.yml` (houserules.default-token-tags-start-no-workflows records the mechanism). The pipeline would cut a tag and a draft release and upload zero artifacts, silently.

Two documented fixes, either closes the gap: (a) pass a PAT or GitHub App installation token as `release-please-action`'s `token:` input, so the tag push carries a real identity; (b) add a `github-script` step to release-please.yml, gated on the action's `release_created` output, that calls `workflow_dispatch` on release.yml directly, needing no PAT.

OWNER-ATTENDED: the choice is a secrets-management and workflow-ownership decision, not a technical unknown. Blocks the first real release-please release from actually publishing binaries; HR-049 and HR-063's live re-verification (spec 7's step two) wait on it. T2's runbook release section must name HR-068 so the owner meets the decision where the release is performed.
Source: batch 19 task 1 review, issue 3 (2026-09-06).

items.title: Narrow check-report-claims' paste-run lint: quote-aware placeholder, $(...)-aware tokenizer
body: Batch 20 T2 fix round 1 review, important findings 3-4: the paste-run lint (HR-071) ships with two measured false-positive vehicles, both disclosed as Limits bullets in crates/houserules/src/report_claims.rs rather than narrowed. (1) The appended-annotation check's subshell exemption only covers a `(...)` wrapping the WHOLE command; a chained `cmd1 && (cmd2)` reads as an appended annotation instead — .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-04-batch-17/task-2-report.json live_run[8] is a real instance the shipped checker flags. (2) The placeholder check ignores quote_mask's state entirely, so a quoted angle-bracket literal that is command DATA (an HTML-comment probe, or a `Co-Authored-By: ... <email>` trailer this repository's own standing no-coauthor rule guarantees will keep generating) misreads as a placeholder — the lint's most frequent false positive at filing time: 5 instances across 4 workspace reports.

The narrowing: (a) a quote-aware placeholder arm in find_placeholder, skipping any span quote_mask already marks as inside a quoted string; (b) a $(...)-aware tokenizer arm in quote_mask, tracking that a same-character quote re-opened inside a `$(...)`/`` `...` `` command substitution starts a fresh, independent quoted region rather than closing the one around the whole substitution (the vehicle report_claims.rs's own Limits section discloses from batch 20 T2's first pass, 2 instances in that same review's own corpus sweep). Deferred per process.no-tech-debt: both are bounded, well-scoped engineering — quote_mask already carries the byte-level state the placeholder check would need to consult, and the $(...) arm needs a small quote-context stack, not a rewrite — not a correctness blocker for HR-071's shipped form, which already discloses both gaps with their measured instances rather than shipping them silently.

items.title: release-please's release-type still needs the package.json HR-047 retired
body: PRE-MERGE: this fires on the next push to main, not at a later release attempt. Batch 20 T3 (HR-047, docs/specs/2026-09-07-batch-20-phase5.md §2) retires package.json along with the rest of the JS toolchain. release-please-config.json's packages['.'].release-type is still "node", with no package-name override, and .github/workflows/release-please.yml runs release-please-action@v5.0.0 on every push to main -- not only when cutting a release.

Derived from the pinned v17.11.2 source (release-please-action@v5.0.0 resolves release-please ^17.6.0), not a config-string reading, per process.wiring-checks-run-the-resolution: BaseStrategy.buildReleasePullRequest calls getBranchComponent() to name the release branch. Unlike its sibling getComponent(), getBranchComponent() is NOT guarded by includeComponentInTag -- it always calls getDefaultComponent(), which falls through to `this.packageName ?? getDefaultPackageName()` since no package-name is configured. The Node strategy's getDefaultPackageName() reads package.json through getPkgJsonContents(); a missing file makes getPkgJsonContents() catch FileNotFoundError and throw MissingRequiredFileError naming package.json, 'node', and this repository.

HR-068 (the tag-push token gap) does NOT shield this: HR-068 is about release.yml never starting after a tag pushes, which happens strictly later in the pipeline than this failure. Once T3's branch merges, release-please-action throws on that very push, before any PR opens -- not gated behind HR-068/HR-069's step-two release track, and not something a later release attempt discovers first.

Re-scoped as a pre-merge owner decision (fix round 1, task-3-review.json important finding 4 -- the original wording hedged the impact as 'may fail ... or error outright' and scheduled it behind HR-068/HR-069, which the derived call path above shows is wrong on both counts). The choice among a different release-type (rust: needs the workspace root to carry a [package]; simple: needs a version.txt this repository does not have) or node with an explicit package-name pointing at a file that still exists is a config ruling this checkout cannot close: it needs a real release-please run against the chosen config, not a source reading alone.
Source: batch 20 T3 (HR-047) implementation, discovered while removing package.json per spec §2; re-derived and re-scoped in fix round 1 (task-3-review.json, important finding 4).

RULED 2026-09-08 (design.md 5.43): release-type rust at crates/houserules, landed on the batch-20 branch pre-merge; plain v-tags kept; extra-files re-derived; local validation as far as possible, live proof at the owner-attended first release.

APPLIED 2026-09-08 (batch 20 T5). release-please-config.json's packages["crates/houserules"] now names release-type "rust" (packages['.'] and "node" gone); .release-please-manifest.json's key moved with it. extra-files: the redundant crates/houserules/Cargo.toml toml/jsonpath entry is gone (the Rust strategy already emits that update natively, source-verified); README.md and template/.github/workflows/knowledge.yml now read /README.md and /template/.github/workflows/knowledge.yml (a leading / anchors an extra-file to the repository root once the package sits off root -- BaseStrategy.addPath, v17.11.2 source, docs/runbook.md's HR-073 section carries the file:line citations). changelog-path: "/CHANGELOG.md" keeps the existing root changelog rather than letting the strategy start a second one under crates/houserules/. items.title: release-please misses commits that change the embedded template/ payload but not crates/houserules/**
body: HR-073's release-type: rust at crates/houserules moved release-please's commit attribution off the repository root: CommitSplit.split (commit-split.ts:99) now counts a commit toward the crate's next version only when it touches crates/houserules/**, since the ROOT_PROJECT_PATH special case that used to assign every commit (manifest.ts:700-701) no longer applies. crates/houserules/src/install.rs:232-234 embeds `../../template/` into the shipped binary via #[derive(RustEmbed)], so a commit that changes only template/ (or README.md, or another root-level path) changes shipped code and, under the new attribution, opens no release PR at all.

Measured over v0.2.0-alpha..9e4bf91 (batch 20 T5 fix round 1 review): 82 of 119 commits touch no path under crates/houserules/, and 7 of 27 feat/fix commits are unattributed under the new package path -- four of them (9a3d697c feat(template), 523da2f0 fix(template), 1537d89a fix(tools), 6fb46ca4 fix(template)) change the embedded payload directly, per t5-evidence/hr081-template-payload-commits.sh's own enumeration by touched path rather than commit subject (fix round 2: a subject-scoped read of the same range missed 1537d89a, 'fix(tools): validate rejects incomplete terminal reports', which touches no crates/houserules/ path and two template/ files). Today enough crate-side commits ride along that a release PR still opens; a cycle whose only changes are template/, README.md, or the knowledge base would silently ship nothing.

The package path is not the thing to change: release-type rust at '.' (the root) would take the Rust strategy's workspace branch and push a CargoToml update for the root manifest, which cargo-toml.ts:37-40 throws on ('is not a package manifest') since the root Cargo.toml carries no [package] section under this workspace's virtual-manifest shape -- reviewer-confirmed and re-verified by the implementer. The gap needs a different remedy, not a reversal of HR-073's ruling.

Candidate remedies (this item carries the question, not the answer): (a) an extra-files or component-mapping addition to release-please-config.json that attributes template/** changes to the crate's own path for commit-attribution purposes; (b) a documented pre-release rule that a payload-changing commit always rides alongside a crate-side commit before a release is cut, checked by hand or by a gate. Owner picks.
Source: batch 20 T5 fix round 1 review (task-5-review.json), important finding 1.

items.title: Cargo.lock's houserules version line goes stale after a release-please merge, no owner yet
body: HR-073's release-type: rust config gives Cargo.lock no extra-files entry: the Rust strategy's own built-in Cargo.lock update (rust.ts:124-128) targets addPath('Cargo.lock') under the package's own path -- crates/houserules/Cargo.lock, which does not exist, since this repository's real Cargo.lock sits at the workspace root -- so the update silently no-ops (github.ts:850-861) and a release-please merge bumps crates/houserules/Cargo.toml's version without touching Cargo.lock's own recorded entry for the same package.

Verified live (batch 20 T5, and re-verified in fix round 1 with a bounded, rerunnable sweep, t5-evidence/ci-lock-flag-sweep.sh): no --locked/--frozen/--offline flag exists anywhere in this repository's own CI surface (.github/, mise.toml, dist-workspace.toml) or in cargo-dist v0.32.0's own build path (cargo-dist/src/build/{cargo,mod,fake,generic}.rs), so any subsequent cargo build/check/test invocation -- including the one dist build runs when cutting a release -- silently rewrites the stale line to match Cargo.toml, with no failure anywhere today.

The risk: a --locked consumer would fail outright. Reproduced live (bumping the crate's version in this checkout, running the command, then reverting): `cargo check --locked` fails with 'cannot update the lock file ... because --locked was passed' (t5-evidence/cargo-check-locked-fails.log). Nothing in this repository's pipeline runs with --locked today, so this is a latent risk, not an active break -- but it has no tracked owner now that HR-073 is ticked done, and process.no-tech-debt wants an accepted gap carried by a backlog item, not by a closed one's body.

Candidate remedies (open): extend the post-release-please-merge restamp procedure (docs/runbook.md) to also run a Cargo.lock refresh (e.g. `cargo update -p houserules --precise <version>` or a plain `cargo check`) and commit it alongside the kit-version restamp; or accept the residue indefinitely with this item standing as its documented risk record. Filed separately from HR-081 (same review round, same closed item, different mechanism -- a stale lockfile line versus a missed release PR -- so a remedy for one does not gate the other).
Source: batch 20 T5 fix round 1 review (task-5-review.json), minor finding 3.

items.title: Windows CI's first real run finds tests/fixtures/** CRLF-corrupted, breaking two check_parity byte compares
body: HR-083's mise pin unblocked mise-action's setup step on every ci.yml job, so windows-latest's `rust` job ran `cargo test` for real for the first time in this batch (every earlier CI attempt on this branch, and on 0399758 before it, failed at mise-action before cargo test ever started there) -- this is a first real signal, not a regression HR-083 introduced. Two check_parity.rs tests failed there: `check_knowledge_matches_the_frozen_mini_corpus` (stdout diverged: actual "" against the frozen `knowledge: ok\n`) and `check_knowledge_matches_the_frozen_mini_stale_corpus` (stderr diverged: the actual run additionally flags `.claude/rules/standing-rules.md` as stale, absent from the frozen golden, and reports `CLAUDE.md: 14279 bytes` against the frozen `14257 bytes`) (batch 20 T6, t6-evidence/pr8-post-fix-rust-windows-FAIL-job-log.txt, run 34215459708 job 102026042204).

Root cause, confirmed for the mini-stale byte divergence: `tests/fixtures/mini-stale/CLAUDE.md` is 14257 bytes on a Linux checkout (`wc -c`, matching the frozen golden exactly) and `git check-attr text` reports it "unspecified". `.gitattributes` already marks `tests/corpus/**` and `tests/goldens/**` `-text` for exactly this failure class -- its own comment cites the identical break on PR #6, run 34056471594 -- but nothing protects `tests/fixtures/**` the same way, so the windows-latest runner's default `core.autocrlf` converts every fixture file's checked-out LF to CRLF, growing CLAUDE.md by 22 bytes and flipping standing-rules.md from current to stale because its checked-out bytes no longer match a freshly rendered copy bit for bit.

The `mini_corpus` failure (empty stdout in place of `knowledge: ok\n`) is not root-caused to the same certainty and is recorded as observed, not diagnosed further, per knowledge-base.state-only-the-source.

Candidate fix (ready, mirrors the two existing `.gitattributes` entries): add `tests/fixtures/mini/** -text`, `tests/fixtures/mini-bad/** -text`, and `tests/fixtures/mini-stale/** -text`; the same reasoning also reaches `tests/fixtures/batch14-workspace/** -text`, today equally unprotected despite houserules.corpus-batch14-fixtures-are-committed's own "verbatim" intent. Re-run the windows-latest leg live before closing this item.

Blocks a fully green windows-latest leg on batch-20's PR #8. Filed separately rather than folded into HR-083: batch 20 T6's own scope was the mise pin alone, one commit, and this is an unrelated root cause (git line-ending checkout behavior, not action version resolution).
Source: batch 20 T6, the live CI run after the mise-pin fix (t6-evidence/pr8-post-fix-rust-windows-FAIL-job-log.txt).

FIX ROUND 1 (batch 20 T6, controller re-scope: implements in this batch, process.every-main-commit-is-ci-green). True root cause, traced through git history rather than left as the candidate guess above: these seven fixture directories lived under tests/corpus/fixtures/ and so carried tests/corpus/** -text (batch 16 T1, commit 950eaf0) until batch 20 T3's relocation (commit 850559c, "chore(tests): relocate tests/corpus/fixtures to tests/fixtures") moved them to tests/fixtures/ without a matching .gitattributes update -- a rename path rules do not follow, not a gap that predated Windows consumers. Landed as tests/fixtures/** -text (commit 2d1f3fc), covering all seven relocated directories at once (git add --renormalize changed zero files -- every blob was already pure LF). Both named failures are fixed and reverified live: check_parity.rs carries no failure in any windows-latest run since.

The mini_corpus mechanism is now confirmed, not merely observed: check.rs's check_base does an exact string compare between each on-disk generated file (.claude/rules/*.md, the knowledge skill) and a freshly rendered LF copy, and check_budget counts raw bytes/lines -- CRLF-inflating mini's own generated files creates a spurious stale finding, and check-knowledge prints empty stdout for ANY finding (confirmed against tests/goldens/check/mini-bad.json, whose golden stdout is also ""), exactly matching the observed empty-stdout symptom. Same cause as the byte-count divergence, one fix (tests/fixtures/** -text) covers both, as predicted.

Two further, previously-hidden windows-latest layers surfaced and were fixed in the same fix round, each only reachable once the layer before it stopped aborting cargo test early (plain `cargo test` stops at the first failing binary): (1) commit_msg_hook.rs's hook_path() built its path through Path::canonicalize, which the pinned rustc 1.98.1's own docs confirm produces a Windows-only `\\?\`-prefixed extended-length path incompatible with an external command-line consumer -- Git-for-Windows' sh could not open it, exit 127 on all 7 tests, run 34217792336 job 102033559639; fixed (commit 3942892) by building the path directly from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR without canonicalizing. A fourth, structurally different failure remains after all three fixes (install.rs's init_reports_a_render_failure_on_broken_project_data_as_one_usage_error, run 34218918139 job 102037165620): filed separately as HR-085, since its mechanism is not CRLF/git-checkout at all (the seeded broken JSON is written at runtime via fs::write, never through git) and was not confidently root-caused despite substantial tracing. windows-latest is not green yet; the batch's merge remains blocked on HR-085.
